initial_requirements: Wind-power operators need a standardized communication system for remotely supervising and operating turbines supplied by different vendors. The system should transfer measurements, status information, alarms, and other plant data to authorized operational applications and carry commands or settings back to individual turbines or wind-farm controllers. It must serve different authorized parties while keeping communication failures from disrupting the safe local operation of the plant.

messages.content: What are the primary business and operational goals this standardized wind-turbine communication system must achieve, and how will you define success for the project?

The main goal is to let operators supervise and control turbines from different vendors through one standardized way of communicating, instead of having separate solutions for each supplier. Operationally, it has to reliably move measurements, status, alarms, and commands between the turbines, wind-farm controllers, and authorized applications without compromising safe local operation if communication is lost.
We would consider it successful if operators can use it across mixed-vendor sites with fewer integration issues, consistent access to plant data, and dependable command handling under normal and degraded network conditions. It should also be clear that a communication failure does not create unsafe turbine behavior, and that only authorized parties can access the right functions and data.
